continuity.narrative_arc: Storm crossing and infant exchange; Kamsa learns of the girl and threatens her; Yogamaya manifests and warns him; Kamsa convenes the asuras; Gokula celebrates Krishna’s birth; Yashoda mothers the infant; Nanda offers gifts and prayer.
continuity.palette_arc: Start in midnight indigo, storm blue, dark river and painted ochre; transition through muted prison stone and Yogamaya’s restrained violet-gold divine light; close in warm cream, mineral ochre, deep maroon and muted village greens.
continuity.series_style: Traditional matte South Indian temple-mural: firm dark contours, broad mineral pigment fields, full-bleed no outer frame, shallow decorative space, natural warm-brown human skin, deep indigo infant Krishna; painted ochre ornament, no metallic gloss.
continuity.identity_rules: Infant Krishna remains a natural newborn with exactly two arms in D039. Vasudeva, Devaki, Yashoda, Nandagopan, Kamsa, gopikas and Brahmins are ordinary two-armed humans. Yogamaya alone has the specifically required eight-arm divine form in S005-S006; each arm connects clearly to her body.
continuity.source_policy: D039 reference images guide scene composition only. Do not imitate their photorealistic/glossy styles or reproduce watermarks/UI. D039/008 is the lead S008 source; D039/009 is preserved as a secondary S008 source because its numbered caption is also 8.
continuity.portrait_policy: All portrait compositions are recorded as future independent recompositions; portrait generation is paused for this assignment.
continuity.bhattathiri_policy: S010 keeps the poet’s closing prayer in the devotional light/gaze of the scene; Bhattathiri is not inserted as a participant in the historical Gokula ritual. If later requested, use the existing older clean-shaven identity contract exactly.
